International Baccalaureate Candidacy

Candidate School for the IB Primary Years Programme

PSG World School is a candidate school for the International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme. Candidacy is an important stage in our development as a school shaped by inquiry, reflection, international-mindedness and meaningful action.

Candidate status does not guarantee authorisation. Only schools authorised by the International Baccalaureate Organization may offer an IB programme.

Who Chooses PSG World School

Families who are done waiting
for a school like this

Coimbatore's globally minded families have always known what great education looks like — they just haven't always found it here. PSG World School brings together international standards, future-ready learning, and the trust of the PSG legacy in one place.

🏭

Industrial & Business Families

Textile, manufacturing, and entrepreneurial families who want more than academic scores alone — they want confident communicators, ethical leaders, and globally capable children prepared for the future.

🩺

Healthcare Professionals

Doctors, specialists, and healthcare leaders who value balanced child development, inquiry-based learning, and a school culture that supports both wellbeing and high expectations.

💻

IT & Startup Professionals

Tech founders, innovators, and senior professionals seeking a modern education that develops creativity, problem-solving, collaboration, and real-world future skills — not outdated rote learning.

🌍

International Families

Families relocating from abroad or moving between countries who want continuity, international standards, and a welcoming school community that understands global transitions.

🔄

Families Seeking a Fresh Start

Parents looking beyond traditional rote-learning schools and searching for a more engaging, future-focused educational experience with strong transition support and individual attention.

A Message from the Head of School

When families choose a school, they are making far more than an educational decision. They are choosing a community that will help shape how their children understand themselves, relate to others, and engage with the world around them.

That belief has guided my work across Ireland, the United States, Sweden, Bangladesh, Thailand, Myanmar, Russia and India. Different countries, cultures and systems have convinced me of one thing: great schools help young people become both capable and good.

At PSG World School, we are building a learning community grounded in strong values, curiosity and meaningful relationships. We want students to grow not only in knowledge and capability, but also in the confidence to ask questions, the courage to take initiative and the wisdom to use their talents in service of something larger than themselves.

I am delighted to welcome you to PSG World School and to invite you to be part of this exciting journey.

IgniteCuriosity fuels discovery. We encourage learners to ask questions, explore ideas and develop a lifelong love of learning.
InnovateCreativity drives progress. We empower students to think critically, embrace new perspectives and develop solutions to meaningful challenges.
InspireCharacter shapes impact. We nurture integrity, compassion and purpose, inspiring students to make a positive difference.
David William Sheehan
Founding Head of School

How We Think About Education

How Learning Happens

The Inquiry Journey —
from question to real-world impact

Learning often begins with a meaningful question and can lead to thoughtful action.

01

Question

What do we want to understand? Students develop questions rooted in curiosity and connected to clear learning goals.

02

Investigate

Students research, explore, observe and gather evidence from appropriate sources and experiences.

03

Create

Students develop an explanation, design, product, performance or proposal with a clear purpose.

04

Feedback

Students share work with peers, teachers and, where appropriate, relevant audiences for specific and useful feedback.

05

Improve

Students reflect, revise and present. Important work develops through more than one attempt.

Many units may culminate in a public product or presentation, giving students a purposeful audience for their learning. The form and audience depend on the age of the learners and the goals of the unit.

Learning in Action

Real questions.
Purposeful work.

These planned examples show how authentic inquiry may develop from Grade 1 to Grade 5. Final products, audiences and community contributors will be confirmed as units are designed and implemented.

Grade 1 · Curious Explorers

Sensory Stories

Driving question: How can we create a story that can be experienced in more than one way?

Students explore texture, shape, colour, sound and sequence, then design and improve a tactile story page, sensory panel or interactive storytelling experience.

Possible outcomeTactile storybook or sensory story experience
Learning focusStorytelling · Empathy · Making · Reflection
Lead Care Worker · PSG Vishnugranthi Day Care Centre
Grade 2 · Community Makers

A Water-Wise School

Driving question: How can our school reduce unnecessary water use?

Students observe where water is used, record simple information, identify opportunities for improvement and design child-friendly messages that encourage responsible use.

Possible outcomeCampaign, illustrated signs and observation report
Learning focusObservation · Measurement · Responsibility · Action
Siruthuli Environmental NGO + PSG World School Facilities Manager
Grade 3 · Design Thinkers

An Inclusive Campus Study

Driving question: How can our school spaces work better for everyone?

Students examine routes, signs, seating, lighting, sound, visibility and ease of movement. They identify possible barriers, gather feedback and develop practical recommendations or simple prototypes.

Possible outcomeIllustrated study with recommendations and prototypes
Learning focusEmpathy · Evidence · Design · Improvement
CCMC Ward Officer, Peelamedu
Grade 4 · Storytellers and Changemakers

Voices of Coimbatore

Driving question: Whose stories help us understand Coimbatore?

Students prepare respectful questions, gather oral histories and connect personal experiences to wider changes in the city, learning to listen and represent others responsibly.

Possible outcomeAudio exhibition, story collection or local-history display
Learning focusResearch · Listening · Communication · Storytelling
Grace Welfare Trust · Shanthi Nilayam, Peelamedu
Grade 5 · Leaders and Investigators

Clean Air and Safe Journeys

Driving question: How can our school community support safer and healthier journeys?

Students study maps, observe travel and traffic patterns from safe, supervised locations, gather age-appropriate information and develop evidence-based recommendations.

Possible outcomeSafe-journey map, recommendations and awareness campaign
Learning focusInvestigation · Data · Citizenship · Leadership
Peelamedu Traffic Police Station
Planned learning examples. Final audiences, products and community contributors are subject to confirmation.

How Learning is Assessed

Assessment helps children grow —
not fear mistakes

We assess progress continuously — not just through tests.

✎

Teacher Feedback

Specific, regular feedback linked to learning goals helps students understand what is working and what to improve next.

↔

Peer Feedback

Students learn to give structured, kind and useful feedback—developing communication, judgement and responsibility.

◉

Self-Reflection

Children learn to evaluate their own work, recognise progress and identify an appropriate next step.

⊞

Portfolios & Evidence

Portfolios collect selected drafts, feedback, revisions and final work so growth can be seen over time.

◈

Ongoing Check-ins

Teachers check understanding during learning and adjust instruction, grouping or support in response.

★

Unit Evaluations

End-of-unit assessments provide evidence of what students understand and can apply independently.

Additional Growth Evidence

MAP Growth

PSG World School plans to use NWEA MAP Growth, where developmentally appropriate, as one additional source of evidence alongside classroom assessment, portfolios and teacher observation.

The adaptive assessment is designed to help teachers identify current strengths, areas for growth and progress over time. It does not replace teacher judgement or define a child’s potential.

The implementation schedule and grade coverage will be communicated clearly to enrolled families.

⊞

Adaptive questions

Questions respond to a student’s answers so the assessment can gather useful evidence across a range of attainment.

↑

Growth over time

Repeated measures can help teachers and families see progress, not only a single attainment point.

◉

Planned checkpoints

The timing and participating grades will be communicated to families as part of the school assessment calendar.

✎

Informs teaching

Results are considered alongside classroom evidence to support differentiation and appropriate next steps.

Families will receive regular evidence of learning through student portfolios, reports and purposeful conversations with teachers.

The Learning Continuum

Opening with Early Years
through Grade 5

The 2026–27 opening phase includes Early Years 1–3 and Grades 1–5. Later stages shown below are part of the school’s long-term development and remain subject to phased implementation, regulatory approvals and relevant programme authorisations.

Early Years 1–3
Ages 3–6 · Currently offered
Play & Discovery
  • Child-led play and exploration
  • Language and early literacy
  • Social and emotional foundations
  • Creative and sensory learning
Lower Primary
Grades 1–3 · Ages 6–9 · Currently offered
Inquiry & Foundations
  • Transdisciplinary units of inquiry
  • English, Mathematics and Tamil
  • Arts, Music, Movement and PSPE
  • Developing research and thinking skills
Upper Primary
Grades 4–5 · Ages 9–11 · Currently offered
Depth & Agency
  • Deeper conceptual understanding
  • Increasing student ownership
  • Digital literacy and citizenship
  • Community-connected learning
Planned Middle School
Grades 6–10 · Ages 11–16 · Future phase
Identity & Increasing Rigour
  • Subject-specialist learning
  • Critical and analytical thinking
  • Service and leadership opportunities
  • Pathway subject to future approvals
Planned Senior School
Grades 11–12 · Ages 16–18 · Future phase
Excellence & Purpose
  • Advanced study and independent research
  • University and career guidance
  • Personal responsibility and service
  • Pathway subject to future approvals
